column1: # The ESCAPE HATCH, and nothing else. Empty is the normal state.
# This lane's subject is the REFERENCE HAND PORT's own MUnit suite run against the mechanically
# emitted `sge.ai.*` (`PROGRESS.md` §10.7.12). It runs NO migration, so it has no
# `run-latest/dropped-types.tsv` and nothing here can be DERIVED — which is exactly why the row
# below has to be stated rather than left to a mechanism, and exactly why it is a claim someone
# has to defend.
# THE ROW IS ONE FACT, AND IT IS A HAND-PORT DIVERGENCE, NOT AN ENGINE GAP. `Task.cloneTask()` in
# java instantiates the task reflectively (`com.badlogic.gdx.utils.reflect.ClassReflection
# .newInstance`) and, for a type with no visible nilary constructor, javac's own contract raises
# `ReflectionException` which `cloneTask` wraps in the `TaskCloneException` it declares
# (`Task.java:266-272`). This port keys that on a `Class`-value registry whose `miss` reproduces
# the JVM's reflection AND its failure — `Miss.JvmReflect(OnFailure.Throw("sge.ai.btree
# .TaskCloneException", …))` with `handles = ReflectionException`, so java's now-dead handler is
# elided exactly (`RegistryTransform`, `ENGINE-LIMITS.md` P10 wave 3). `CountingTask` takes a
# constructor argument, so THE PORT NOW DOES WHAT JAVA DOES: it raises `TaskCloneException`.
# The test still fails because it asserts a SUCCESSFUL clone, which java cannot deliver either.
# The REFERENCE port answers the same question differently: it added an abstract `newInstance()`
# member to `Task` so that cloning needs no reflection at all, and the suite's `CountingTask`
# overrides it. That is a REDESIGN of the library's surface, not a translation of it — so this
# test asserts the hand port's answer against the mechanical port's, and java's own source is the
# oracle where the two disagree (CLAUDE.md §3.5: behaviour — java wins). The suite's fixtures
# still DECLARE `newInstance()` (mapping row M7 drops only the `override` keyword, since this
# port's `Task` has no such member to override); what they cannot do is make this port's
# `cloneTask()` call it.
# WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ROW WRONG. If the hand port's `newInstance()` divergence gets a verdict and
# a NAMED spelling here (an `AddMembersTransform` member plus a `cloneTask` body, or the row is
# ruled a hand-port defect and the fixture is adapted), this test passes and `test-failures.tsv`
# reports the declared row for deletion. If a DIFFERENT failure appeared, `frame=` stops holding
# and it counts UNEXPECTED — which is the whole reason the frame is here. The frame is the MINTED
# registry, because that is where java's own refusal is now raised.
# `test` may be `*` to declare a whole suite.
#suite
sge.ai.btree.TaskSuite
column3: CountingTask declares no nilary constructor, so the registry's JvmReflect arm raises the TaskCloneException java's own contract raises there (Task.java:270); the hand suite asserts a successful clone, which it can only get from the reference port's ADDED Task#newInstance() -- a hand-port divergence, not an engine gap.
